questions.prompt: Which expression is the threshold voltage of an n+ poly / p-Si MOS capacitor?
options: \(V_T = V_{FB} + 2\varphi_p\)
\(V_T = V_{FB} - 2\varphi_p + \frac{1}{C_{ox}}\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_sN_A(-2\varphi_p)}\)
\(V_T = -2\varphi_p + C_{ox}\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_sN_A}\)
\(V_T = V_{FB} - \frac{1}{C_{ox}}\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_sN_A(-2\varphi_p)}\)
questions.explanation:
Three terms: flatten the bands (\(V_{FB}\)), bend the silicon by \(-2\varphi_p\), and drop \(|Q_B|/C_{ox}\) across the oxide to support the depletion charge.
Note \(\varphi_p < 0\), so \(-2\varphi_p > 0\).

options: It decreases: the |Q_B|/C_ox term halves, while V_FB and −2φp are unchanged
It doubles
It's unchanged, because V_T depends only on doping
It increases, because the field is stronger
questions.explanation: Only the oxide term depends on \(t_{ox}\): \(\frac{|Q_B|}{C_{ox}} \propto t_{ox}\). For our device it goes from 0.242 to 0.121 V.

questions.prompt: Doubling \(N_A\) changes all three \(V_T\) terms. Which changes the most (for \(N_A \sim 10^{17}\), \(t_{ox} = 5\ \mathrm{nm}\))?
options: \(-2\varphi_p\), which doubles
\(V_{FB}\), which doubles
None change
The \(|Q_B|/C_{ox}\) term, which grows roughly as \(\sqrt{N_A}\); \(V_{FB}\) and \(-2\varphi_p\) change only by about \(V_{th}\ln2\)
questions.explanation:
Logarithmic terms: \(\Delta(-2\varphi_p) = 2V_{th}\ln2 \approx 36\ \mathrm{mV}\) and \(\Delta V_{FB} = -18\ \mathrm{mV}\). Square-root term: \(\times\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt{1+\ldots}\), about \(+0.11\ \mathrm{V}\) here.
Gotcha: doubling the doping does NOT double \(V_T\).

questions.prompt: For p-type silicon, \(\varphi_p = -0.419\ \mathrm{V}\) (\(N_A = 10^{17}\)). A student plugs this into \(V_T = V_{FB} + 2\varphi_p + |Q_B|/C_{ox}\). What goes wrong?
options: Nothing; the two forms are equivalent
V_T comes out 0.42 V too high
The sign is wrong: the band bending must be \(-2\varphi_p = +0.838\ \mathrm{V}\), so their \(V_T\) comes out about 1.68 V too low
Only V_FB is affected
questions.explanation:
Bending the surface from \(\varphi_p\) to \(-\varphi_p\) takes \(-2\varphi_p > 0\). Writing \(+2\varphi_p\) subtracts 0.838 V instead of adding it, a 1.676 V error.
Gotcha: sign slips with \(\varphi_p\) are the most common \(V_T\) error. For n+/p, every term except \(V_{FB}\) should be positive.

questions.prompt: A body bias \(V_{SB}\) adds to the needed silicon drop, changing \(|Q_B|\) to \(\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_sN_A(-2\varphi_p + V_{SB})}\). For the \(N_A = 10^{17}\), \(t_{ox} = 5\ \mathrm{nm}\) device with \(V_{SB} = 1\ \mathrm{V}\), by how much does \(V_T\) rise, in V?
questions.explanation:
\[\Delta V_T = \frac{\sqrt{2q\varepsilon_sN_A}}{C_{ox}}\left(\sqrt{-2\varphi_p + V_{SB}} - \sqrt{-2\varphi_p}\right) = \gamma(\sqrt{1.838} - \sqrt{0.838})\]
\[\gamma = 0.264\ \sqrt{\mathrm{V}} \Rightarrow \Delta V_T \approx 0.116\ \mathrm{V}\]
Gotcha: the change goes as a square root, not linearly with \(V_{SB}\).

questions.prompt: Preview of body bias: the reverse source-to-body bias \(V_{SB}\) raises \(V_T\) as above. Where does this matter in circuits?
options: Only in PMOS transistors
In stacked transistors (e.g. the upper NMOS in a NAND gate or a source follower), whose sources sit above ground, so their V_T is higher
Nowhere; the body is always tied to the source
Only in the oxide breakdown rating
questions.explanation: Any NMOS whose source is not at the body (ground) potential sees \(V_{SB} > 0\). This 'body effect' reduces the drive and the gain of a source follower.

questions.prompt: Preview of PMOS: for a p+ poly gate on n-type silicon, what's the sign of \(V_T\), and what gate voltage turns the device on?
options: V_T is negative; the gate must go below V_T (more negative) to invert the n-surface into a hole channel
Positive, like NMOS
Zero always
Negative, but a positive gate turns it on
questions.explanation: Everything mirrors: \(\varphi_n > 0\), so the band bending is \(-2\varphi_n < 0\), and the depletion charge is positive donors, so the oxide term is negative. Holes form the channel.
